question: In 2021 and 2022, the Commission worked with a consultancy to develop a study on intersex people in the EU, which was originally scheduled to be released in late 2022. The study was ultimately completed in spring 2023 and a preliminary presentation of the report on the study was made in May 2023 to the IDAHOT+ Forum by the consultancy firm ICF S.A.

The contract with the consultancy preparing the study ended shortly thereafter in 2023, and the Commission indicated to civil society in July 2023 that the study was complete and undergoing internal validation. However, the report itself remains unpublished. 1.
Why has the report on the study on intersex people in the EU still not been released?
When will the Commission release the report on the study on intersex people in the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.6.2024) The LGBTIQ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, intersex or queer) equality Strategy 2020-20251 pays particular attention to the diversity of LGBTIQ people’s needs and to the most vulnerable, including intersex people.

In particular, the strategy foresees fostering exchanges of best practices on the legal protection of intersex people against discrimination and on ending intersex genital mutilation, and to gather evidence on the barriers that prevent intersex people from achieving full equality.

The Commission commissioned a study on intersex people in the EU to provide a comprehensive analysis and overview of the socio-economic position and inclusion of intersex people and the possible correlation between their socio-economic position, their health status and the applicable legal framework.
The assessment and the validation process concerning the study is ongoing given its comprehensive scope and the complexity of the areas covered.
